profile.address: Fairway Meadows Apartments, Hales Camp, Smyrna, Rutherford County, Middle Tennessee, Tennessee
profile.reading:
The Tennessee South Data Center sits in Smyrna, in Rutherford County southeast of Nashville, and is part of the State of Tennessee's own information technology operations rather than a leased commercial property. Public project documentation from ABEC Electric, the electrical contractor engaged to build the facility's power infrastructure, describes a building of roughly 50,000 square feet with about 25,000 square feet configured as raised floor data center space, completed around 2016. That contractor record also details dual utility feeds into the site, dual 2 megawatt generators arranged in a paralleling configuration for backup power, and redundant uninterruptible power supply systems, a combination consistent with a facility built to keep running through a single utility outage or generator failure.

No Tennessee state government source has published an official critical IT load figure in megawatts for the facility, so while the generator sizing gives a sense of the backup power envelope, it does not by itself establish how much of that capacity is dedicated to running servers versus supporting cooling, lighting, and other building loads. That is a common gap in public records for government data centers. Contractors who built the electrical plant will describe what they installed, but the agency operating the finished building rarely publishes a separate operational capacity figure of its own.

One naming confusion is worth clearing up directly. There is a separate Tennessee State Data Center associated with the University of Tennessee, Knoxville, but that is the state's affiliate site in the U.S. Census Bureau's State Data Center program, a network that distributes census and demographic statistics to researchers and the public. It has nothing to do with physical server infrastructure and should not be confused with this Smyrna facility, which is real estate housing actual state government computing equipment.

Rutherford County has grown rapidly as part of the Nashville metro area over the past two decades, and Smyrna in particular has attracted industrial and logistics investment, including a major Nissan manufacturing plant nearby, which speaks to the area's utility and workforce infrastructure. Locating a state government data center there, rather than directly in Nashville, fits a broader pattern of state agencies siting sensitive infrastructure outside the densest parts of a capital region while staying close enough for staff and connectivity. Beyond the building's size, floor configuration, and backup power description from the electrical contractor's own project record, no further technical or capacity detail about the Tennessee South Data Center is publicly available.

reading.body:
The Tennessee South Data Center in Smyrna is a state-operated facility completed around 2016 with approximately 25,000 square feet of raised floor data center space. Backup power infrastructure includes dual 2 megawatt generators in a paralleling configuration, though no published figure for critical IT load capacity was found from a tier one state source. The facility has dual utility feeds and redundant UPS systems.

No certification or compliance statement was published by the operator for this facility. The data center's intended uses and tenant profile therefore cannot be read from public specifications.

Among the 24 mapped data center facilities in Tennessee, only 4 have published megawatt figures from operator spec pages. This facility ranks fifth among those with published figures in the state, though the published figure of 4 MW capacity is not an official critical IT load statement. Tennessee's four published facilities total 12.13 megawatts, placing the state among the lower-capacity states tracked by this project.
